title: Carl Ballantine and Johnny Kuhlman
summary: Riddick tells how the magician Carl Ballantine turned to a comic act; Allen asks about Kuhlman as a singer.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: It says Matthe. M-A-T-H-E. Matthe. Vagabond artist. M-A-T-H-E. Accent of U on the E.

Now, this guy... What was his name? The great... Anyway, he was on this... In this show... With Ernest Borgnine and this submarine. They had a submarine, you know, it was on that series, television and everything.

Mac Hales Navy. Mac Hales Navy. All right. This guy called... What caused this guy to do what he did? He was a real fine magician. But he wasn't making a dime. He told me the whole story. And he got real sick. Laying in the hospital, he got to thinking. He said, suppose I make a comedy act out of it and foul up everything that I do. The great Ballantine, that's his name. Carl Ballantine. So, he got out there and everything that he did, he fouled up. It didn't work. But he made such a to-do out of it that he went over like a house afire. And this guy, he's still working. And that's a long time ago. And one of the nicest fellas you ever knew in your life. Now, I don't know what this is. It might not be anything. Well, that's something. No. Johnny Kuhlman. From John Kuhlman. Oh, that's a picture. I don't know what I've done with a picture. He's Kuhlman's dead, you know.

Yeah. Well, he was a singer, too. Did you ever hear him sing? Johnny? No. I never heard him sing once, but I know he used to sing. I think I've even seen pictures of him on the band. I hear him down the wall.
